lines: Progressive dyspnea, orthopnea, and palpitations over 2 days
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Kindergarten teacher.
On examination, her blood pressure is 110/70 mmHg, heart rate is irregularly irregular at 120 bpm, respiratory rate is 22 breaths/min, and oxygen saturation is 94% on room air.
Auscultation of the heart reveals a diastolic rumbling murmur best heard at the apex with an opening snap.
Chest X-ray demonstrates pulmonary venous congestion and an enlarged left atrium.
An electrocardiogram shows atrial fibrillation with no ST changes or T wave abnormalities.

encounters.cc: Routine prenatal visit at 20 weeks gestation with questions about influenza vaccination

lines: Routine prenatal visit at 20 weeks gestation with questions about influenza vaccination

The patient is a 30-year-old female with alpha-thalassemia trait and rheumatic mitral stenosis initially diagnosed in January 2020 following an emergency department presentation with progressive dyspnea, orthopnea, and palpitations, who returns for routine prenatal care.
She is currently at 20 weeks' gestation in her first pregnancy.
Her prenatal course has been uncomplicated, and she reports no symptoms today.
She recalls receiving the flu shot a couple of years ago but has not yet been vaccinated this year.
She expresses concern about receiving vaccines during pregnancy and asks if she should wait until after delivery.
Her vaccinations are up to date, including Tdap and MMR prior to pregnancy.
She takes only a prenatal vitamin.
She works as a kindergarten teacher and is concerned about being exposed to illnesses from her students during the winter season.

encounters.cc: Routine obstetric evaluation at 28 weeks gestation

lines: Routine obstetric evaluation at 28 weeks gestation
Patient with alpha-thalassemia trait and rheumatic mitral stenosis returns for prenatal visit at 28 weeks with no significant complaints during the pregnancy and denies recent illnesses or trauma.
There is no evidence of maternal diabetes or alloimmunization.
- Uncomplicated pregnancy without urinary tract infection (diagnosed 2022-07-15)
There is no family history of genetic conditions
The patient and her partner are both originally from Thailand.
Routine serologies for infections including Toxoplasma gondii, cytomegalovirus, and parvovirus B19 are negative.
Noninvasive prenatal testing did not show any chromosomal abnormalities.
Ultrasound reveals a fetus with significant abdominal fluid accumulation, bilateral fluid collections in the chest cavity, and a small amount of fluid around the heart.
Amniotic fluid volume appears normal, and fetal growth parameters are within the expected range.
The neonatology team is consulted, and maternal peripheral smear is sent for evaluation.

encounters.cc: Burning pain and tingling over the lateral right thigh for 2 months

lines: Burning pain and tingling over the lateral right thigh for 2 months

The patient is a 30-year-old female with alpha-thalassemia trait and rheumatic mitral stenosis who returns to the obstetrics clinic for continued prenatal care following her routine evaluation at 28 weeks gestation, presenting with a 2-month history of burning pain and tingling over the lateral aspect of her right thigh.
She denies any recent trauma or injury to the area.
She mentions that the symptoms are exacerbated by standing for long periods and are relieved when lying down.
She has gained 25 pounds during her pregnancy.
- Uncomplicated pregnancy without urinary tract infection (diagnosed 2022-07-15)
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Kindergarten teacher.
On physical examination, there is no erythema or edema, but there is a distinct area of decreased sensation over the anterolateral aspect of the thigh.
Hip and spine examinations are normal.
Deep tendon reflexes are intact, and straight leg raise test is negative bilaterally.

encounters.cc: Progressive swelling and discomfort in left leg over 3 days

lines: Progressive swelling and discomfort in left leg over 3 days
This 31-year-old with alpha-thalassemia trait and rheumatic mitral stenosis presents during pregnancy with left leg symptoms.
She reports difficulty walking due to tightness and aching pain that worsens with prolonged standing.
She has no history of trauma or recent travel.
- Uncomplicated pregnancy without urinary tract infection (diagnosed 2022-07-15)
Her pregnancy has been uncomplicated thus far, and she has attended all scheduled prenatal visits.
She does not use tobacco, alcohol, or drugs.
On examination, she is afebrile with stable vital signs.
Her left calf is visibly swollen and tender to palpation compared to the right.
There is mild erythema but no skin breakdown or ulceration.
Compression ultrasonography reveals a noncompressible left popliteal vein consistent with deep vein thrombosis.

encounters.cc: Decreased fetal movements over the past 24 hours

lines: Decreased fetal movements over the past 24 hours
The 31-year-old with rheumatic mitral stenosis and alpha-thalassemia trait presents in her third trimester with decreased fetal movements, one month after DVT.
She reports that the baby used to be very active, especially after meals, but she has felt only a few movements since yesterday morning.
She denies any vaginal bleeding, leakage of fluid, or contractions.
The patient is visibly concerned and asks about the health of her baby.
- Uncomplicated pregnancy without urinary tract infection (diagnosed 2022-07-15)
- Deep vein thrombosis of left lower extremity in pregnancy (diagnosed 2023-01-15)
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Kindergarten teacher.
Blood pressure is 120/78 mmHg, heart rate is 88 bpm
On examination, fetal heart rate auscultated by Doppler is 140 bpm.
There is no abdominal tenderness, and the uterus is appropriately sized for gestational age.
Her prenatal labs have been unremarkable, and her glucose challenge test was normal.
31-year-old female with alpha-thalassemia trait and rheumatic mitral stenosis returns to the emergency department with a 6-hour history of recurrent decreased fetal movements.
She has had an uneventful pregnancy until now, with regular prenatal care.
- Uncomplicated pregnancy without urinary tract infection (diagnosed 2022-07-15)
- Deep vein thrombosis of left lower extremity in pregnancy (diagnosed 2023-01-15)
- Decreased fetal movements in third trimester (diagnosed 2023-02-15)
Her first child was delivered vaginally at term without complications.
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Kindergarten teacher.
Blood pressure is 120/75 mmHg, pulse is 80 beats per minute, and temperature is 36.8°C (98.2°F)
Fetal heart rate monitoring shows minimal variability with no accelerations and occasional late decelerations.
An ultrasound is performed, which reveals oligohydramnios.
A biophysical profile is conducted, yielding a score of 4/10 (non-stress test: 0/2, fetal breathing movements: 0/2, fetal movements: 2/2, fetal tone: 2/2, amniotic fluid volume: 0/2).

encounters.cc: Regular contractions every 3 minutes and labor arrest after water broke

lines: Regular contractions every 3 minutes and labor arrest after water broke
Patient with rheumatic mitral stenosis and alpha-thalassemia trait returns in labor following emergency department visits.
She reports that her water broke 2 hours ago.
After 5 hours of adequate contractions, the patient is now experiencing intense pain and requests pain relief.
- Uncomplicated pregnancy without urinary tract infection (diagnosed 2022-07-15)
- Deep vein thrombosis of left lower extremity in pregnancy (diagnosed 2023-01-15)
- Decreased fetal movements in third trimester (diagnosed 2023-02-15)
- Fetal distress (Category III fetal heart rate tracing) (diagnosed 2023-03-15)
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Kindergarten teacher.
On admission, her cervix is dilated to 6 cm, 90% effaced, and the fetus is at a -2 station.
The fetal heart tracing is reassuring. a repeat cervical exam shows no change in dilation, effacement, or station. she has no signs of infection
